subject: Scaling residency handshake — EU onshore + APAC warm-standby for upcoming renewal
messages:
From: Sam Clarke <sam.clarke@healthlane.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthlane.com, ops@healthlane.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 08:12:00 +0200
Subject: Renewal window — EU onshore residency and APAC warm-standby ask

Hi Naomi / Ben,

Quick context: renewal for HealthLane's account HL-2027-0423 is up Nov 1. Our legal and security teams have new language requiring an EU-onshore data residency guarantee for PHI subsets and an APAC warm-standby for peak traffic during our APAC pilot (Q1).

Key asks up front:
- Confirm whether Redwood can provide an EU-onshore tenancy (single-tenant or onshore mirror) that meets our data residency attestation.
- Estimate delta for adding APAC warm-standby (cold-to-warm boot in <= 15m) and approximate monthly committed units for the standby pool.
- Include a suggested test cadence for cross-region failover and rollback windows (we'll need a test during the renewal onboarding).

We'd like a short mutual action plan and rough numbers by EOD Thursday so procurement can fold into the renewal SOW. Attaching our internal expected traffic table.

Attachments: capacity_table_Q3.xlsx (traffic peeks and retention tiers)

Thanks,
Sam Clarke
Head of Platform Ops — HealthLane

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Clarke <sam.clarke@healthlane.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:40:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Renewal window — EU onshore residency and APAC warm-standby ask

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear outline.

Short answers:
- We can offer an EU-onshore residency variant (customer-managed VPC + onshore mirror) with an attestation package (SOC2 summary + residency declaration).
- APAC warm-standby is feasible as a reserved warm pool; typical cold->warm target is 10-15 minutes depending on model family and cache warming.
- We'll propose a 60/30/10 test cadence (60% read-only failover validation, 30% simulated traffic, 10% full failover) during a dedicated 4-hour window — we can refine.

Next steps I propose:
1) Redwood to produce a two-page residency amendment and delta TCO (delta for onshore + warm-standby).
2) Ben to propose pricing tiers and committed capacity options.
3) Monica to own the runbook and post-test validation steps.

I've attached a draft capacity table (you sent theirs back annotated) and flagged the most likely SKU bump line items.

Attachments: capacity_table_Q3.xlsx (annotated by Redwood)

On timing — we'll try to get the MUTUAL ACTION PLAN (short form) to you by Friday COB. If procurement needs earlier numbers we can give a ballpark.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Customer Success Manager — Redwood Inference

--

Thanks Ben — quick clarifications from our side:
- Residency warranty: legal is pushing for a contractual warranty on residency for the PHI subset (not just an attestation). They will sign off on attestation only if the SLA contains a rollback guarantee and indemnity carve-out.
- Warm-standby sizing: We'd like the standby pool to cover 30% of peak APAC traffic for 2 sustained hours with automated KV warming. The attached traffic table clarifies peaks.
- Failover tests: We need documented rollback steps and a success threshold for warm-standby (99% request pass for two consecutive 15-min windows).

Procurement looped in for contract language — they'll need the residency amendment and the pricing sketch by Friday so they can draft the renewal SOW.

Sam
Head of Platform Ops — HealthLane
